Products and shapes of tensors

Source: R/ops.R
zl-shape.Rd

zl_crossprod(a, b) is crossprod(a, b): for a of dims c(K, M) and b of c(K, N) it has dims c(M, N), batched over the third and fourth dimensions (where a's may divide b's). A linear layer stores its weight as c(n_in, n_out) and computes zl_crossprod(w, x); the weight may be stored as f16 or bf16.

Usage

zl_crossprod(a, b)

zl_reshape(x, dim)

zl_permute(x, perm)

zl_t(x)

zl_cont(x)

zl_view(x, dim, offset = 0)

zl_concat(a, b, axis)

zl_pad(x, after)

zl_get_rows(x, idx)

Arguments

a, b, x

Tensors.

dim

New dimensions: one to four positive whole numbers.

perm

A permutation of seq_len(k), with k at least the rank of x and at most 4.

offset

The first element of the view, counting from 0.

axis

The dimension to join along, from 1 to 4.

after

Numbers of zeros to append after each dimension.

idx

An integer input (declared with zl_int()) of column indices.

Value

A tensor.

Details

zl_reshape() gives new dimensions with the same number of elements; zl_permute() reorders dimensions as aperm() does; zl_t() transposes the first two; zl_cont() makes a permuted tensor contiguous (operations do it themselves when they need to); zl_view() is a window of prod(dim) elements from position offset (counting from 0) of a contiguous tensor. zl_concat() joins two tensors along axis, zl_pad() appends zeros after each dimension, and zl_get_rows() selects columns of a matrix (rows in 'ggml”s terms) by an integer input, counting from 0. zl_concat() and zl_pad() have no gradient.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "w", c(4, 2))
g <- zl_graph(
  function(x) zl_t(zl_crossprod(zl_param_tensor(p, "w"), x$x)),
  p,
  inputs = list(x = c(4, 3))
)
dim(zl_forward(g, list(x = matrix(1, 4, 3)))$output)
#> [1] 3 2
